claims.text: The initial material is an as-cast polycrystalline FeCoNiTi high-entropy alloy.
The as-cast FeCoNiTi alloy contains both fcc and hexagonal C14 Laves phases.
The alloy exhibits ferromagnetic transitions at approximately 1084 K, 214 K, and 168 K.
The fcc phase is responsible for the transitions at 1084 K and 168 K.
The C14 Laves phase is responsible for the transition at 214 K.
The fcc phase has a notably high coercive field.
Targeted heat treatment can increase the fcc phase fraction and modify its magnetic characteristics.
A slight adjustment of Ti content can increase the fcc fraction or beneficially modify its magnetic characteristics.
The high coercivity of the fcc phase is enhanced by magnetocrystalline anisotropy.
Ti-induced antiferromagnetic coupling contributes to the magnetocrystalline anisotropy of the fcc phase.
Multiple ferromagnetic transitions produce larger magnetic entropy changes during application and removal of a magnetic field.
High magnetic anisotropy in the fcc phase produces larger magnetic entropy changes during magnetic-field cycling.
Heat treatment and minor compositional tuning can enhance the magnetocaloric effect relative to the untreated alloy.
Increasing the fcc phase fraction and optimizing its magnetic properties will increase magnetic entropy change near the transition temperatures.
The unmodified as-cast alloy has suboptimal magnetocaloric performance.
The baseline magnetocaloric performance is suboptimal because its phase balance and magnetic anisotropy are insufficiently controlled.
Magnetocaloric enhancement is conditional on increasing the fcc fraction and shifting its transition temperatures into an optimal range.
If treatment does not beneficially change the fcc fraction and transition temperatures, magnetocaloric performance will remain similar to baseline.
